A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUDA framework and main experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original attribution accuracy, runtime measurements, qualitative examples, and ablations on CIFAR-10 and UnlearnCanvas.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds anchor ablations, likelihood-oracle comparisons, and noisy-group experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, ELBO-difference attribution, preservation losses, ReTrack redirection, and conditional style-selection anchors are retained. The density-ratio correction changes the theoretical derivation; v2 explicitly states that the practical loss still omits this factor.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10 and UnlearnCanvas coverage is retained. Appendix D.6 adds an imperfect-grouping scenario by randomly reassigning 5% of CIFAR-10 group membership, extending evaluation beyond clean semantic groups.

E2.justification: V2 adds uniform style sampling and style-removed conditioning as evaluated comparison variants against AWSS in Table 3. The external comparator sets in the original main experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces supplementary evaluation against a PF-ODE likelihood oracle with aligned batching, a balanced 5% group-corruption protocol with retrained LOGO models, and controlled anchor comparisons. It also revises the stated conditional-unlearning learning rate from 1×10⁻⁶ to 2×10⁻⁶ in Appendices B.1 and C.2.2; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: Three substantive analyses are added: whether weighted retain-style anchors outperform simpler alternatives (B.1), whether ELBO attribution agrees with likelihood-based attribution (D.5), and whether attribution withstands noisy group membership (D.6). The earlier hyperparameter, aggregation, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new PF-ODE analysis averages likelihood estimates over five independent Hutchinson seeds, synchronized across models. The noisy-partition experiment specifies seed 42. These add seed and stochastic-estimation reporting, but neither version reports confidence intervals or repeated-training uncertainty for the main comparisons.

E6.justification: Main-table accuracy values are retained, while substantial new results appear in Tables 3, 13, and 16. Anchor Top-1 scores are 0.456 for AWSS, 0.447 for uniform sampling, and 0.400 for style removal. Under the new likelihood oracle, GUDA leads DAS on Top-1 (0.645 versus 0.639), but trails on NDCG@3 (0.618 versus 0.630). Under noisy groups, GUDA achieves 0.673 Top-1 versus DAS's 0.666.

T1.justification: V1's Appendix A.1 claims an unbiased retain-only reformulation without the sampling density ratio. V2 inserts p_ret/p_for into Equation 15 and distinguishes that exact objective from the implemented approximation in Section 4.2.1. This substantively repairs the central mathematical justification. Appendix C.3.5 also corrects the truncated RBO range from [0,1] to [0,1−p^N].

C1.justification: The central contributions and approximately 100× CIFAR-10 speedup claim remain. V2 narrows causal wording to group-removal counterfactual effects and recasts the conclusion around best or tied-best head-focused metrics. The conclusion also strengthens its general runtime claim from reduced cost to an order-of-magnitude reduction over LOGO.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly defines counterfactuals as operational model comparisons rather than structural causal counterfactuals. It interprets likelihood-oracle results as exposing weaker broader-ranking fidelity and adds substantive limitations concerning omitted density correction, absent approximation-error bounds, hierarchical or overlapping groups, and soft reweighting (Appendices D.5 and E). These substantially expand v1's qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 adds a GUDA code-repository link in the abstract and implementation details for the new likelihood evaluation, including batch size 64, 16 GPU shards, torchdiffeq, and solver tolerances of 10⁻⁵. It also revises the documented conditional-unlearning learning rate. Most existing implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Datamodels (Ilyas et al., 2022) and music attribution through unlearning (Choi et al., 2025), explaining their relationship to GUDA. V2 more explicitly locates novelty in LOGOA, oracle validation, and conditional anchors while acknowledging ReTrack reuse. Numerous publication-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted wording and terminology edits, expands related-work and theoretical explanations, corrects cross-references, and adds acknowledgements, a conflict disclosure, and a limitations appendix. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the anchor, likelihood-oracle, and noisy-partition tables; Table 13(a) also redisplays existing results. Existing figures are retained with label and annotation edits, including corrected style names. Tables and figures move through pagination while the overall document format remains stable.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs a central mathematical justification and distinguishes the implemented approximation from the exact objective. New anchor ablations, likelihood-oracle validation, and noisy-partition tests address important evidence gaps in v1, while expanded limitations improve interpretation. These substantially strengthen correctness and validation. Remaining reporting weaknesses include the unexplained learning-rate revision and the conclusion's broad order-of-magnitude speedup claim, since Table 2 supports only about 5.2× on UnlearnCanvas.
